chunks: 4059 - Al-Sakuni narrated from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

“Ali عليه السلام ruled regarding a man who left his animal due to hardship. He said: If he left it in pasture, water, and safety, then it remains his, and he may take it wherever he finds it. But if he left it in a place of danger, without water and without pasture, then it belongs to the one who finds it.”

key_terms.أَصَابَهَا: found it or came upon it
key_terms.السَّكُونِيُّ: Al-Sakuni, the narrator transmitting this report
key_terms.خَوْفٍ: danger or a state of risk
key_terms.قَضَى: issued a legal judgment or ruling

ai.seo_question: When does an abandoned animal remain the property of its owner in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about an abandoned animal and whether the original owner retains ownership. If the animal was left in conditions where it could survive safely, it remains the owner's property; but if it was left in peril without the means of survival, it becomes the property of the one who finds it.
